title: X-ray and Gamma-Ray Astronomy
welcome_lead: Hot plasmas, jets and the highest-energy events.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: Chandra, XMM-Newton, Fermi and high-energy astronomy.
final_note: Earth's atmosphere blocks high-energy photons — go to space.

walkthroughs.body_html: X-rays cannot be focused by ordinary mirrors — they need grazing-incidence nested shells. Chandra and XMM-Newton, both 1999, image hot plasma in clusters and accretion disks.
Gamma rays cannot be focused at all — instruments measure where each photon strikes. Fermi (2008) maps high-energy sources including pulsars, AGN and gamma-ray bursts.
Earth's atmosphere absorbs X-rays and gamma rays entirely — happily for life on the surface. Useful observations require satellites high above it.
